heroHeadline: Day 9,002 of America's Longest War — Op Ghazab Day 95; 26-Day Strike Pause; Eid al-Adha & TTP Ceasefire Imminent; Jawid Niazi Day 25 in Taliban GDI; Afghanistan Hosts 20,000+ Terrorists
heroSubtitle: May 31, 2026 marks Day 9,002 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom on October 7, 2001. Day 95 of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq continues with no confirmed cross-border airstrikes for a 26th consecutive day since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike. Eid al-Adha 2026 is imminent — TTP leader Noor Wali Mehsud's announced 3-day ceasefire (10th–12th Dhu al-Hijjah, expected June 6-7) will briefly pause TTP attacks in KPK. Pakistan Today, The Express Tribune, and The Nation reported on May 30 that UN Security Council Monitoring Team and Russian FSB data characterize Afghanistan under Taliban rule as 'evolving into a terror exporter' hosting 20,000–23,000 terrorists across 20+ organizations — with ISIS-K (2,000-3,000 fighters) actively recruiting in Central Asia and among Russian migrant workers. This assessment comes just 72 hours after Russia and the Taliban signed a Military-Technical Cooperation Agreement (May 27-28) — a strategic paradox reflecting Moscow's dual-track approach. Paigard News Agency director Jawid Niazi remained in Taliban GDI custody on Day 25 — no bail, no charges, no confirmed legal access. TOLOnews journalists Mansoor Niazi and Imran Danish remain on bail pending trial after Eid. No Urumqi Round 2 date announced; China silent on mediation since April 8. WFP urgently needs $313M as 4.9M Afghan mothers and children face malnutrition.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA, Express Tribune, Pakistan Today, ISPR, Xinhua, CPJ, Amnesty International, Afghanistan International, Amu TV, The Diplomat, WFP, Moscow Times, RFE/RL, Pajhwok, Khaama Press, The Nation
